correctness.rationale: For real functions on any finite connected positive-weight graph, the weighted coarea equality decomposes TV into cut boundaries. Every coordinate permutation maps cardinality-k level sets to cardinality-k level sets, giving a universal J_k/I_k bound. Sorting along a line segment is continuously piecewise a coordinate permutation, which preserves the bound. Strict rank-separated base inputs plus indicator perturbations map any minimizing cut to any maximizing cut of the same size and attain the bound, so the formula is sharp. All singleton and all doubleton cuts prove the uniform-clique rigidity, with n=2 separately. Direct cut enumeration proves path/cycle/star/barbell formulas. A standalone exact-rational checker ran from the newly assembled file path and independently confirmed 43 small connected simple graphs, 24 weighted graphs, 11 family sizes and five barbells. Finite checks are not substituted for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The exact claim is a two-input nonlinear BV sensitivity modulus for global rank sorting on arbitrary finite connected positive-weight graphs, plus nonexpansivity rigidity and quadratic barbell amplification. The most pertinent primary rearrangement theorems establish one-input inequalities TV(Rf)<=c TV(f), which neither imply nor are implied by a bound on TV(Rf-Rg)/TV(f-g). A separate weighted-graph cut functional from published graph zonotope work concerns a minimal cut/Euclidean normalization, not maximal-to-minimal equal-cardinality cut ratios or rank sorting. The known coarea and chamber-permutation ingredients are expressly not claimed as new. Earlier implicit versions remain a bibliographic risk; novelty is best-knowledge qualified.

value.rationale: This determines the exact Lipschitz modulus of a natural nonlinear rank-statistic map on every finite connected graph with arbitrary positive edge weights. The answer is an intrinsic ratio of edge-isoperimetric profiles and is attained for each fixed cardinality. The criterion L=1 if and only if uniformly weighted complete graph is a full rigidity classification, while barbells of 2q vertices have L=floor(q^2/2)+1, revealing unexpected quadratic two-input BV instability despite familiar single-input rearrangement smoothing and coordinatewise lp nonexpansiveness. The formula and extremal family are structurally motivated, not arbitrary numerical slices; computational complexity limitations are disclosed.
